title: AI Whistleblower: We Are Being Gaslit By AI Companies, They’re Hiding The Truth! - Karen Hao
description:
The truth about Sam Altman. AI Critic Karen Hao reveals what 90 OpenAI employees told her.

Karen Hao is an AI expert, award-winning investigative journalist, and former reporter for The Wall Street Journal covering American and Chinese tech companies. She is also co-host of the podcast The Interface and freelances for publications like More Perfect Union and The Atlantic. Her latest book is the bestselling ‘EMPIRE OF AI: Inside The Reckless Race For Total Domination.’

She explains:
◼️Why the US-China “AI arms race” may be misleading and politically driven
◼️Why AGI is a marketing scam used to consolidate trillion-dollar power
◼️The hidden human cost behind AI training

top_comments.author: @GigiGreen29
top_comments.text: As someone who has recently gotten an MBA degree from a top USA University and has struggled to find employment for more than a year after graduation, this conversation is fascinating. Especially because I've seen the two sides of the coin of the haves and the have-nots. When you sit down to talk about business decisions, return on investments, what the future is gonna look like after a particular technology is deployed, etc, the people sitting on the table making the decisions have NO IDEA of the reality of the working class and just take the reality of their surroundings as true for everybody else, like Steven saying he sees people getting more connected in the future because of AI. And the thing is, when your life is comfortable, it is just hard to imagine what life looks like for people who do not have the same privileges as you have. And I know that because in my years in business school and working for a few of these huge companies, the impact that their operations and business decisions have is very frequently reduced to how much more profit they are going to have, and maybe trying to mitigate any backlash in case they make a wrong move. It's easy to not hire a human being because an AI machine can deliver a better service when you have no idea of the consequences of unemployment on so many people's lives.  It's just too distant. You are "safe", riding your autonomous car and having every single one of your needs met. And this is not a judgment on anyone, it's just that humans are generally too self-involved to care about the other (me included). Fair to say that we cannot count on business leaders to make sound decisions for society as a whole.
